shape: Cherry cluster (3 platforms joined by narrow stems)
description: Three discrete platforms connected by narrow stem corridors — like a cluster of three cherries. The south platform (where spawn_south arrives) is joined to the west/north platform by a single narrow stem at the north-west corner; the west platform is joined to the east/south platform by a longer stem from its south-east corner. Each platform has corners wired as a clique so objectives anywhere on it can be reached from the entering anchor. The voids between platforms are NOT walkable.

portals.north: spawn_north at (-20.03, -12.66) — south side of the west platform's SW corner

traversalNotes: MULTI-PLATFORM TOPOLOGY: three discrete platforms (south, west, east) joined by narrow stems. Between platforms is void — STRICT-BACKBONE applies: do not emit cross-platform edges except via the explicit stems south_plat_nw ↔ west_plat_ne and west_plat_se ↔ east_stem_west ↔ east_plat_sw.
Direct south → north: spawn_south → south_plat_ne → south_plat_nw → west_plat_ne → west_plat_sw → spawn_north. Five hops, hopping the south-to-west stem.
Direct north → south: reverse of the above.

EAST PLATFORM is OFF the south-north route — only reached from the west platform via the longer stem. Reaching anything on the east platform requires: current_gate → backbone → west_plat_se (gyl1) → east_stem_west (xm8v) → east_plat_sw (x5bj) → east-platform corner → reverse.

PER-PLATFORM CLIQUE: each platform's four corners form a clique so the autopilot can reach any corner objective regardless of which corner it entered from. The dispatch rule is the same as I/arena stages but the dispatch hub is the entering-corner anchor, not a single center anchor.

FENCE / SWITCH HINT: the stems (south-west and west-east connections) are narrow and frequently gated. Expect fences on either stem and a switch on the originating platform (the one the autopilot must traverse first). Pre-switch routing: visit every corner of the originating platform looking for the switch before attempting the stem traversal.
Stages are never physically rotated — all positions here are stage-local mesh-space XZ.
